messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D open-world martial arts game where the player can use the environment to hurt NPCs.

## Requirements
- Main character is a martial artist; open-world gameplay; environmental hazards can be used against NPCs.
- Build the game now without clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Created an original lantern-lit district sandbox, “Iron Lotus — Night Market,” using Three.js from a CDN.
- Implemented keyboard/mouse controls and responsive touch controls; NPCs are challengers in a non-lethal sparring setup.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a 3D district with plazas, streets, landmarks, gardens, a canal, lanterns, and environmental props.
- Added player movement, strikes, dash, grab/toss, NPC pursuit and combat, environmental damage, HUD, minimap, and start/pause/result screens.
- `node --check game.js` passed; opened the local site and saved a start-screen screenshot.

### Active
- Validate the actual gameplay in-browser, including movement, combat, environmental damage, and mobile controls.

### Blocked
- Browser check has only captured the start screen so far; gameplay has not yet been exercised.

## Next Move
1. Click “STEP INTO THE NIGHT” in the browser and verify the game renders and plays without runtime errors.
2. Test movement, strike, grab/toss, NPC damage, and environmental interactions; fix any issues found.
3. Save and inspect a current gameplay screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and HUD structure.
- `style.css`: Visual design and responsive controls.
- `game.js`: Three.js world, player/NPC logic, combat, and controls.

## Important Context
- Local server is running at `http://localhost:3002`.
- `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` succeeded; screenshot saved at `/tmp/opencode/iron-lotus-start.jpg`.
- Browser reported a missing `/favicon.ico` (404) and WebGL performance warnings; no gameplay errors have been checked.
- Changes are uncommitted.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D open-world martial arts game where the player can use the environment against NPCs.

## Requirements
- Main character is a martial artist; open-world gameplay; environmental hazards can be used against NPCs.
- Build the game without clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Created “Iron Lotus — Night Market,” an original Three.js district sandbox using Three.js from a CDN.
- NPCs are challengers in a non-lethal sparring setup.
- Strike and grab targeting select the nearest challenger regardless of facing, then turn the player toward them.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the lantern-lit district, landmarks, gardens, canal, buildings, and environmental props.
- Implemented movement, strikes, dash, grab/toss, NPC pursuit and combat, HUD, minimap, and start/pause/result screens.
- Added keyboard/mouse and touch controls.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Browser tests confirmed strikes, grabbing, and tossing work; NPC attacks reduce player vitality.
- Confirmed mobile controls appear and touch grab/toss can be used in gameplay; no browser console errors in the latest checks.

### Active
- Verify NPC knockback into environmental hazards causes bonus damage and the environmental impact toast.
- Thoroughly validate mobile movement and combat behavior; movement input was exercised, but results were inconclusive.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test knockback into a hazard and confirm `ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT  ·  BONUS DAMAGE`.
2. Continue validating mobile movement and touch combat, fixing issues if found.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and HUD structure.
- `style.css`: Visual design and responsive controls.
- `game.js`: Three.js world, player/NPC logic, combat, and controls.

## Important Context
- Local game URL: `http://localhost:3002`.
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear as untracked in `git status --short`.
- Gameplay screenshots: `/tmp/opencode/iron-lotus-gameplay.jpg`, `/tmp/opencode/iron-lotus-mobile.jpg`; a mobile movement test screenshot is `/tmp/opencode/iron-lotus-mobile-move.jpg`.
- Environmental damage is implemented in `damageEnemy()` and `breakHazard()` in `game.js`, but has not yet been confirmed in browser testing.
